items.t: 78 houses sold in Grandview, Surrey at a median of $1,782,500 (middle half $1,526,250 to $2,041,250). A typical house in Grandview, Surrey spent 42 days on the market and closed at 96.1% of the asking price.
In Grandview, Surrey, townhomes sold at a median of $829,900 across 203 sales, and the middle half closed between $770,000 and $927,500. The median townhome sat 24 days and sold for 97.7% of list.
Grandview, Surrey: 45 condos sold at a median of $565,000, with the middle half between $497,500 and $609,000. The median condo took 28 days to sell and closed at 97.4% of list.

24 duplexes sold in Grandview, Surrey at a median of $1,242,500 (middle half $1,199,975 to $1,279,125). A typical duplex in Grandview, Surrey spent 24 days on the market and closed at 98.0% of the asking price.

How Grandview compares with the rest of South Surrey and White Rock

items.t: Houses in Grandview have the third highest median of 8 South Surrey and White Rock sub-areas, $1,782,500. King George Corridor is lowest at $1,345,000 and Elgin Chantrell highest at $2,280,000. Crescent Beach and Ocean Park ($1,745,000) sits just below and Morgan Creek ($1,960,000) sits just above.

Of 8 South Surrey and White Rock sub-areas with 5 or more townhome sales, Grandview ranks 4th highest at $829,900; the range is $776,000 (King George Corridor) to $1,242,500 (Elgin Chantrell). Pacific Douglas ($825,000) sits just below and White Rock ($885,250) sits just above.

Condos in Grandview have the third highest median of 7 South Surrey and White Rock sub-areas, $565,000. Sunnyside Park Surrey is lowest at $506,500 and Crescent Beach and Ocean Park highest at $1,035,000. King George Corridor ($553,000) sits just below and Elgin Chantrell ($625,000) sits just above.

blocks.text: By build year, duplexes are the newest homes selling in Grandview, Surrey (median 2026) and condos the oldest (median 2010), a gap of 16 years.
